name: Robarts Research Institute
summary: Robarts Research Institute has a curved blue-green glass front between heavy light masonry ends, a long rectangular south wing, and low glazed sections inside the curve.

evidence.note: regional-2m surface heights above inventory ground. Median 19.35 m, P90 33.60 m, highest return 34.74 m.
Original reference colour from a mean image patch centred at (139,119) on a 300 by 300 normalized grid in RRI. Raw sRGB #8f918b. Joint colours and unit sizes estimated.
2025 London orthophoto. Sunlit roof patch at local [228.2, -52.5] averages #c2c8bb.
Light blockwork at the tall end, narrow vertical dark glass slot, reflective curved blue glass wall with small punched windows on its upper band.
Outside of the bend has wide gridded reflective glazing, pale piers, a square-window upper band and low windows against the ground.
Tall near-blind northern bookend with horizontal joints and a vertical reveal beside the reflective glass.
Low glazed pavilion in the foreground of the inner court, mostly hidden behind landscaping at its base.
Tall curved wall and stepped top rise above the low forecourt roof.
Courtyard returns near (265,-92), (272,-102) and (274,-101) are about 0.9 m. These lie below the low roofs at 4.6–6.7 m and the inner face of the tall curved wing.
The inner glazing follows a distinct curved ledge at 24.3–24.4 m from (276,-104) through (274,-96), (272,-92) and (268,-88). The roof immediately behind this ledge returns about 29 m.

notes: Both the public-facing glazed elevation and its roof turn continuously in plan. The polygon approximates the curve with straight segments. Entry position is approximate. Bay counts on obscured faces and dimensions of openings are estimates. The upper glass follows the concave internal courtyard edge between the wings. The dark top screen follows its curve.
